items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to exempting certain parcels of land from the provisions of law which generally restrict manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers from sharing an interest in a liquor license
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6816

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law,
in relation to exempting certain parcels of land from the provisions
of law which generally restrict manufacturers, wholesalers and
retailers from sharing an interest in a liquor license

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL : To allow a developer in the City of
Syracuse to apply for a farm brewery license and a craft microbrewery
license while still operating retail locations in Central New York.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends Section 101(1) of the Alcohol Beverage Control Law
to exempt five properties in Central New York from the State's
"three-tier" law. This will allow the owner to apply for and construct
a farm brewery in the City of Syracuse in a previously abandoned
building.

Section 2: Establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :  The Alcoholic Beverage Control Law prohibits an
establishment with an interest, whether direct or indirect, from
manufacturing and selling product at retail. The original intent of
the law was to encourage competition in the post-prohibition era;
however, in many circumstances it now discourages economic development
and hinders job and tax revenue growth.

This bill will allow a local developer in the City of Syracuse to
renovate an abandoned industrial building into a new farm brewery that
will include manufacturing, hospitality, retail, high-end residential
units, and office space. This exemption will allow his other
businesses (hotels) in the area to keep their retail licenses and sell
products produced at the farm brewery. The exemption is needed because
of the ownership structure of the hotels, mortgages that require the
locations to maintain their separate retail licenses, and the limits
of the current farm brewery law.

The goal of the farm brewery legislation was to encourage the
production and sale of craft beer in New York, as well as encourage
craft beverage tourism. Allowing this exemption, will create a new
tourism destination in the City of Syracuse, facilitate the
redevelopment of a previously unused building, and encourage new
economic activity in the City. The project is estimated to create 38
full time jobs over the first 5 years of operation.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY : None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS : Increased tax revenue.

 EFFECTIVE DATE : Immediately.
